title: Lunar Shift: Fallback Procedures & Quick Ops Notes (scratchpad)
content:
Purpose:
This is a personal scratchpad for the lunar (late-night) on-call shift. Not a canonical runbook — more of a lightweight, chronological cheat-sheet + temporary procedures for emergency fallbacks we resort to when the full runbook is too slow. Keep terse. Add outcomes here for handoff.

When to use this doc:
- High error rates for hosted API (+10% 5m) and immediate SLA risk
- Model auto-fallback not working (requests piling, 503s)
- KV cache corruption symptoms (inconsistent beam outputs across identical prompts)
- Need a fast, reversible mitigation while SRE/serving-runtime digs deeper

Quick triage (first 5 minutes):
1) Check Grafana overview panel (linked above) — look at 5m error rate and p50/p95 latency.
2) Open recent deploys: kubectl get deploy -n hosting | grep serving-
3) Look for rolling restarts in last 15m (kubectl rollout history).
4) Slack alert channel: #prod-alerts — confirm any ongoing incident threads.
5) Send short status to #prod-alerts: "Lunar on-call taking initial triage; collecting metrics; will update in 10"

Common alerts & first actions (shorthand):
- 503 spike (frontend): check upstream model pool healthy endpoints. If pool size 0 -> scale.
  Commands: 
    rcli pool list --env prod | grep pooled-serve
    rcli pool scale --name pooled-serve --replicas 4  (temporary)
- High token latency p95 but healthy error rate: suspect KV cache cold or batching stall.
  Action: force small rolling restart on worker class to flush partial stalls.
    kubectl rollout restart deployment/worker-serve --namespace serving-runtime
  Note: this loses in-flight KV cache; only do if latency > 10s p95 or sustained for >10m.
- Model fallback loop (requests keep routing back and forth): pin routes to last-known-good variant.
  Command: rcli route set --route-id r-123 --policy "pin:model:v1-fallback" --reason "lunar emergency pin"
  Leave a TODO to revert once root cause fixed.

Emergency fallback plan (fastest, reversible):
1) Pin routes to a smaller, cheaper variant (quantized) to reduce memory pressure. Use only for 10–30 minutes.
2) Enable regional spillover to eu-west if us-west capacity saturated (policy must be safe for data).
3) Notify CS for any impacted customers with changed region or quality.

Quick shell snippets (save time):
- tail logs for recent 503s
  kubectl logs -n hosting deploy/gateway --since=15m | grep "503" | head -n 200
- restart a single node in the dedicated pool (quick drain)
  rcli node drain --node-id node-56 --reason "lunar emergency restart"
- verify model variants available
  rcli model list --model t5-xxl | jq '.variants[] | {name,quantized,latency_profile}'

Temporary workaround: KV cache corruption (observed as non-deterministic outputs for same prompt)
- Symptoms: identical requests produce different outputs within seconds; users report hallucination spikes
- Immediate mitigation: disable prefix caching for the affected model route
  rcli route edit --route-id r-456 --cache-prefix false --reason "disable prefix cache until investigation"
- If disabling cache doesn't help, roll back to previous model version (pin) and scale replicas down->up to reinitialize caches.

Customer notification template (short):
"Hi <customer>, we’re investigating increased latency/errors affecting some requests; we’ve applied a temporary mitigation that may change latency or quality slightly. We will follow up with a root-cause and ETA within 2 hours. — on-call (Aisha)"

Handoff summary template (to write at end of shift):
- Status: green/yellow/red
- Actions taken (timestamped): e.g., 01:12 — pinned route r-123 to model:v1-fallback; 01:45 — scaled pooled-serve to 4 replicas; 02:05 — disabled prefix cache on r-456.
- Open items for next shift: list Jira keys, small next steps, who to loop in.
- Attach logs: path or saved gist link.
- If you changed any route pins or scaling, add a revert ticket with deadline.

Example handoff (fill at shift end):
Status: yellow — error rate recovered to baseline after route pin + scale.
Actions: pinned r-123 -> model:v1-fallback (01:12), scaled pooled-serve -> 4 (01:20), disabled cache on r-456 (01:46).
Open items: INF-789 (root cause: OOM on kernel upgrade); follow-up: LR to run quantization regression test, assign to Marcus.

Notes to self (disorganized):
- If you pin a route, include revert in description: "revert by EOD or after root cause"
- Keep rollback window 30–60m for risky changes at night
- Avoid global restarts unless SRE lead signs off (big blast radius)
- Remember: customer-facing CS message must be approved by oncall mentor (Lena) if <2am.

Unresolved / TODO (for follow-up):
- Add small doc to onboard new SREs on quick fallback commands (short cheatsheet) — link to a future doc.
- Create a script to atomically pin+scale with one command (rcli compose?). Speed matters.
- Revisit auto-fallback policy: too aggressive for low-memory nodes (causes flip-flop). Ticketed INF-790.

References / bookmarks I always check:
- Grafana: serving-runtime-overview (linked_artifacts)
- Recent deploy PRs: review PR #1423 (perf kernels) — monitor for related OOMs
- Slack thread: #prod-alerts pin set during incidents (use permalink)

Final: this file is messy by design. Add short bullet outcomes here during the shift and tidy up into Confluence for any persistent procedure. If anything critical, call out in #prod-alerts and page Marcus (pager duty).

-- Aisha
